content.text:
Done. The full test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## What I changed

The spec required validating an E.164 telephone's national-number length against its country code. I found the normalization logic in `OwnerTelephone.toE164(...)`, which previously only enforced the generic E.164 shape (`+` followed by 8–15 digits).

In `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/OwnerTelephone.java`:

- Added a `NATIONAL_LENGTHS` map (a `LinkedHashMap`, longest-prefix first) mapping country code → required national-digit count: `"61" → 9`, `"1" → 10`.
- After the existing E.164 shape check, the code strips the `+`, finds the matching country-code prefix (checking `61` before `1` so they don't collide), and throws `InvalidTelephoneException` — which the existing `InvalidTelephoneExceptionHandler` turns into a **400** — when the national part is the wrong length. Unknown country codes remain permissive (bounded only by the 8–15 E.164 range).

The new acceptance test `errorRejectsWrongNationalLength` (which posts `+61 123` → only 3 national digits) now returns 400, and the existing valid AU mobile flow (`04XXXXXXXX` → `+61` + 9 national digits) still passes.
